overall_summary: Geopolitical escalation between the US and Iran is injecting fresh risk-off pressure across markets. Bitcoin-specific ETF inflows remain supportive, but unresolved tensions and today's Fed minutes keep direction unclear.
key_points: BlackRock-led ETF inflows hit $266M, supporting Bitcoin
BTC rebounds to $63,300 on sustained ETF demand
US-Iran strikes and Hormuz tensions drive oil up 5%+
IMF lifts 2026 global growth forecast to 3.3%
Fed June FOMC minutes due today amid mixed macro data

items.title: BlackRock IBIT Leads $266M Bitcoin ETF Inflows
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded roughly 266 million dollars in net inflows over the past couple of days, with BlackRock's IBIT alone taking in about 209 million dollars on July 7. This marks a sharp reversal after weeks of outflows that had drained billions. Traders should watch these flows closely because sustained institutional buying can provide a strong floor and fuel upside moves in Bitcoin price.
items.impact: Supports higher prices and reduces selling pressure

items.title: Strategy Sells 3,588 BTC but Market Absorbs Sale
items.summary: Major corporate holder Strategy sold around 3,588 Bitcoin worth 213 to 216 million dollars to fund reserves and dividends. Despite the size of the sale, Bitcoin price held steady near 63,000 dollars without a sharp drop. Traders care because it shows current demand is strong enough to absorb large supply without breaking support levels.
items.impact: Limited downside risk from corporate selling

items.title: Bitcoin Rebounds to 63,300 Dollars on ETF Demand
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around 63,300 dollars on July 8 after touching 64,400 dollars overnight, extending a recovery that began early in the month. The move higher has been supported by ETF inflows, short covering, and softer U.S. labor data that lowered rate-hike odds. Traders should monitor whether the 63,000-dollar area holds as a new support zone.

items.title: Fed Releases June FOMC Minutes Today
items.summary: The Federal Reserve will release the minutes from its June 16-17 FOMC meeting at 2 PM ET. Traders are watching closely for any hints on future rate policy, especially after the committee held rates steady at 3.5% to 3.75% last month amid solid growth but elevated inflation. The details could shift expectations for cuts or hikes later this year.
items.impact: Could drive volatility in rates, dollar, and risk assets depending on hawkish or dovish tone.

items.title: IMF Upgrades Global Growth Forecast to 3.3% for 2026
items.summary: The IMF is set to release its July World Economic Outlook Update today at 9 AM ET, projecting global growth at 3.3% for 2026 and 3.2% for 2027. This reflects resilience in the face of geopolitical and trade headwinds. The update highlights a stable but modest outlook that could support risk appetite if confirmed.
items.impact: Positive for global risk assets including Bitcoin as it signals economic resilience.

items.title: US Wholesale Inventories Rise 0.3% in May
items.summary: May wholesale inventories increased 0.3% month-over-month to around $944 billion, beating forecasts and extending a streak of builds. This follows a stronger April gain and suggests businesses are stocking up amid steady demand. The data points to ongoing economic expansion without major overheating signals.
items.impact: Mildly supportive for growth views but unlikely to shift major market moves on its own.

items.title: MBA Mortgage Applications Fall 2.2% Last Week
items.summary: Mortgage applications dropped 2.2% in the latest week as 30-year rates held near 6.58%. Refinance activity weakened notably while purchase apps were softer too. This reflects persistent high borrowing costs weighing on housing demand.
items.impact: Signals continued pressure on housing sector from elevated rates.

items.title: US Launches Strikes on Iran After Hormuz Ship Attacks
items.summary: The US military carried out a wave of strikes on Iranian targets including air defenses, radar sites and IRGC boats after Iran hit three commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran claims it struck US sites in Bahrain and Kuwait in retaliation. The moves shattered a fragile ceasefire and sent oil prices sharply higher.
items.impact: Risk-off across markets, volatility spike, safe-haven flows

items.title: Oil Surges Over 5% on Hormuz Tensions and Iran Oil Ban
items.summary: Brent and WTI jumped more than 5% after the US revoked Iran's general license for oil sales and launched strikes. Traders are pricing in fresh supply risks through the world's most important energy chokepoint. The move adds upward pressure on energy costs and inflation expectations.
items.impact: Higher input costs, inflation concerns, energy sector outperformance

items.title: Trump Says Iran Ceasefire 'Over' at NATO Summit
items.summary: Speaking from the NATO leaders meeting in Ankara, President Trump declared the US-Iran ceasefire agreement is finished while noting talks could still continue. The summit agenda on defense spending and Ukraine is now overshadowed by the Gulf flare-up.

items.title: Iran Claims Strikes on US Bases in Bahrain, Kuwait
items.summary: Tehran said it targeted US military facilities in Bahrain and Kuwait plus the Fifth Fleet naval base after the American strikes. The tit-for-tat exchange raises the risk of broader regional spillover and further disruption to Gulf shipping.
items.impact: Elevated escalation risk, potential for wider conflict
